lemma quotient_partition_refinement {ι κ : Type*} (s : Finset ι) (t : Finset κ)
    (e : ι → T.CauchyQuotient hadd) (f : κ → T.CauchyQuotient hadd)
findings.problem: Partition refinement is restricted to a quasitrace's Cauchy quotient, although its proof uses only general C⋆-algebra positivity and ring identities. Users cannot apply it directly to partitions in another C⋆-algebra without reconstructing this proof.
findings.proposed_change:
Extract a general lemma with this statement, retaining the quotient theorem as a specialisation if desired:

lemma partition_refinement {A ι κ : Type*}
    [CStarAlgebra A] [PartialOrder A] [StarOrderedRing A]
    (s : Finset ι) (t : Finset κ) (e : ι → A) (f : κ → A)
    (he : ∀ i ∈ s, 0 ≤ e i) (hf : ∀ j ∈ t, 0 ≤ f j)
    (heo : ∀ i ∈ s, ∀ j ∈ s, i ≠ j → e i * e j = 0)
    (hfo : ∀ i ∈ t, ∀ j ∈ t, i ≠ j → f i * f j = 0)
    (hes : ∑ i ∈ s, e i = 1) (hfs : ∑ j ∈ t, f j = 1)
    (hc : ∀ i ∈ s, ∀ j ∈ t, Commute (e i) (f j)) :
    (∀ k ∈ s.product t, 0 ≤ e k.1 * f k.2) ∧
    (∀ k ∈ s.product t, ∀ l ∈ s.product t, k ≠ l →
      (e k.1 * f k.2) * (e l.1 * f l.2) = 0) ∧
    (∑ k ∈ s.product t, e k.1 * f k.2) = 1

The existing proof carries over: Commute.mul_nonneg supplies positivity; associativity, hc and the two orthogonality hypotheses supply orthogonality; finite distributivity supplies the sum. Keep the existing CStarAlgebra scope for real-scalar instances used by functional calculus. Do not add Nontrivial A: the proof also handles the zero algebra. Empty partitions force 0 = 1 through hes or hfs, so require no additional nonemptiness assumptions.
findings.benefit: Makes the refinement construction available directly in arbitrary unital C⋆-algebras, independently of quasitraces and their metric quotients, without changing the mathematics or proof strategy.

findings.excerpt:
lemma quotient_partition_refinement_left {ι κ : Type*} (s : Finset ι) (t : Finset κ)
    (e : ι → T.CauchyQuotient hadd) (f : κ → T.CauchyQuotient hadd)
    (hfs : ∑ j ∈ t, f j=1) (r : ι → ℝ) :
    (∑ k ∈ s.product t, r k.1 • (e k.1*f k.2))=∑ i ∈ s, r i • e i := by
findings.problem: Both marginal identities unnecessarily require real coefficients and this particular C⋆-algebra quotient. Their proofs only distribute a fixed scalar over a finite sum and use semiring distributivity; they need neither order nor compatibility between scalar multiplication and multiplication.
findings.proposed_change:
Generalise the pair to the following statements:

lemma partition_refinement_left {R A ι κ : Type*}
    [Semiring A] [DistribSMul R A]
    (s : Finset ι) (t : Finset κ) (e : ι → A) (f : κ → A)
    (hfs : ∑ j ∈ t, f j = 1) (r : ι → R) :
    (∑ k ∈ s.product t, r k.1 • (e k.1 * f k.2)) =
      ∑ i ∈ s, r i • e i

lemma partition_refinement_right {R A ι κ : Type*}
    [Semiring A] [DistribSMul R A]
    (s : Finset ι) (t : Finset κ) (e : ι → A) (f : κ → A)
    (hes : ∑ i ∈ s, e i = 1) (r : κ → R) :
    (∑ k ∈ s.product t, r k.2 • (e k.1 * f k.2)) =
      ∑ j ∈ t, r j • f j

The existing rewrite proofs use precisely Finset.smul_sum, Finset.mul_sum or Finset.sum_mul, and the unit laws, all available under these assumptions. No Module, scalar-tower or scalar-commutation instance is needed. DistribSMul preserves zero, so empty sums remain valid, including the trivial semiring when an empty partition sums to one.
findings.benefit: Provides reusable weighted-refinement identities for complex coefficients and other distributive scalar actions, and for ordinary semirings, without quasitrace or analytic setup.

variable [AddCommMonoid N] [DistribSMul M N] {r : M}

 theorem

theorem Finset.smul_sum {f : γ → N} {s : Finset γ} :
    (r • ∑ x ∈ s, f x) = ∑ x ∈ s, r • f x :=
  map_sum (DistribSMul.toAddMonoidHom N r) f s

variable [NonUnitalNonAssocSemiring R]

lemma sum_mul (s : Finset ι) (f : ι → R) (a : R) :
    (∑ i ∈ s, f i) * a = ∑ i ∈ s, f i * a := map_sum (AddMonoidHom.mulRight a) _ s

lemma mul_sum (s : Finset ι) (f : ι → R) (a : R) :
    a * ∑ i ∈ s, f i = ∑ i ∈ s, a * f i := map_sum (AddMonoidHom.mulLeft a) _ s
